name: Maximus
beta: Jam the hand-sized crack in the corner, stepping onto several shelves en route to a piece left in place, where you hang the rope and descend.
overview: The central crack of three: hand-sized jams within a dihedral that faces right, with ledges breaking it up and a fixed piece near the top.

current.area_walk_in: The path leads about five minutes through the woods, over a small stream, then climbs and divides next to a large boulder that fronts the cliff. Lines one to sixteen are up the right-hand fork, roughly 30 ft; everything else lies beside that boulder on its left.
current.descent: lower off
current.location: the central crack of a trio of cracks

name: May As Well
beta: The opening crack is wide and sits above a little roof; traverse leftward into a second crack. Follow it through pods onto a shelf holding a clump of small trees, then go up again to bigger trees for the descent.
overview: A crack system broken by pods, beginning with a wide crack set on a small roof and finishing on ledges with trees.

current.area_walk_in: The cliff rises about 50 ft above the principal path. Lines one through eight lie on the right where the spur path arrives, and the rest are on its left side.
current.descent: rappel from the bigger trees on the upper ledge, or lower from the neighbouring anchors
current.location: crack system beside Days of Thunder, starting with a wide crack on a little roof

name: Maypop
beta: A bouldery opening move comes first; after that, balance your way up to the anchors.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: Leftmost line, where the approach path arrives at the wall, ten feet from a low overhang

name: Mental Health
beta: Squirm up the narrowing chimney, then use some creative contortions to get onto the face. You can finish on the wall or stay inside the crack, and come down on the chains.
overview: A dihedral beside the amphitheatre's bolted routes, entered through a narrowing chimney.

current.area_walk_in: Cross the wooden footbridge and keep straight; a branch heads right about 20 feet beyond it. Follow that path uphill roughly ten minutes to the wall.
current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Mentor Powers
beta: Some freedom is allowed: here and there you may pass either side of the bolts. Expect two cruxes, with jugs turning up exactly when you need them.
overview: Thin, technical face climbing on an orange wall that leans out slightly, with a few cruxes and well-timed jugs.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: to the left of the beech tree

name: Basecamp
beta: A corner capped by a roof high above its base starts the line: crank outward to a jam on the lip and pull into the corner, which leads to a stance beneath a bigger roof. Return right toward that roof to place protection, surmount it, and round the lip onto a belay terrace. Natural gear on the face above takes you to the rim.
overview: A long, hard route. Climb to the first roof, move out to a jam at its lip, and enter the dihedral above, which leads to a belay under a bigger roof. After passing that roof you finish up the face on natural gear. Allow at least half a day.

current.descent: abseil on two ropes
current.location: About 40 ft left of Which Way is Up, at a dihedral capped by a roof some 20 ft up

name: Hidey Ho
beta: A short chimney leads onto a belay shelf under a big roof; work out across the roof, regain the face, and follow the crack up to a second belay. A short leftward face then a crack bring you rightward again onto a terrace, and a brief slot finishes the route.
overview: A short chimney leads to a belay below a very wide roof. The route works out the roof, follows a crack to another stance, then crosses a short R-rated face to a crack and continues through a slot to the top.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: About 30 ft left of Basecamp, at a short chimney roughly 10 ft from a bulky flake

name: Which Way Is Up
beta: The crack system runs through several roofs and then up a vertical face; a big terrace finishes it, where you rappel from a tree.
overview: The crack system passes through several roofs onto a steep face where gear is poor. The route continues to a big ledge, where a tree serves for the abseil.

current.descent: abseil off a tree
current.location: About 100 ft left of The Quest, round the corner, on a crack system beside a small pond

name: Etrier
beta: Stick-clip the lowest bolt and aid onward under the roof to begin this slopey route.
overview: A slopey line that begins with aid: reach the first bolt from the ground with a stick clip and haul up to the roof.

name: Pink Feat
beta: Leap to a ledge shaped like a U to begin, then pull a stiff mantel and follow the technical wall to a roomy ledge. Rest, then power up the finger-width crack to a further shelf, and finish up a dihedral to the anchors.
overview: Jump onto the ledge, then mantel and work up a delicate wall to a larger shelf below the crack. After a rest, crank the finger-sized split to a further shelf and finish up a suspect dihedral.

current.area_walk_in: Cross the wooden footbridge and keep straight; a branch heads right about 20 feet beyond it. Follow that path uphill roughly ten minutes to the wall.

name: Minas Ithil
beta: Locate a groove at the base for your start, follow it, then straddle the rounded edge to the summit of the pinnacle. Descend by reversing the route.
overview: A small pinnacle climbed by a groove and then the rounded arete above it; descend by reversing the route.

current.descent: downclimb the route

name: Mini Me
beta: Boulder through the first moves, then stay with the crack, which runs from finger size to hand size, to where it ends; continue past chickenheads to reach the anchors.
overview: A short, gently overhanging crack ranging from fingers to hands. Boulder the start, follow the crack to its end, then continue past chickenheads to the anchors.

name: Minimum Creep
beta: Layback the wide crack alongside its bolts; near the second clip, veer left over a string of sidepulls and underclings, then pull through a last bulge to the chains.
overview: Layback the wide crack, which has bolts. Near the second bolt, veer left along sidepulls and underclings, then get over a last bulge to the chains.

name: Moonbeam
beta: A boulder problem gets you to the lowest bolt, then moderate terrain leads easily to the chains.
overview: Along with Sunshine, one of the most popular and easiest routes at the wall. A bouldery start leads to bolt one, after which moderate ground goes up to the chains.

name: Much Ado About Nothing
beta: Easy moves lead up the left-leaning line to the fourth bolt, where a stopper-style crux waits; past it the handholds improve but the feet stay poor all the way to the chains.
overview: Angles leftward up easy ground, meets a hard stopper move around bolt four, then finishes on positive hands with bad footholds.

beta: Follow the bolts up the corner, work through the heavily plated section, then carry on over the roof and past the pebbly bulge to the cold shuts.
overview: A long, sustained line that begins in a crack-and-corner system angled leftward, then crosses a heavily plated stretch, a roof and a knobbly bulge of small stones.

name: Nicoderm
beta: Start as for Nicorette. At the third bolt, step right and slant upward toward the final bolt of Minimum Creep, finishing at its chains.
overview: A short, blank-looking wall defined by mono pulls. It shares its opening with a neighbouring route and finishes on another.

name: Nicorette
beta: Climb the face, then cut hard to the left and get onto the arete, following the bolts to the chains. Reach matters here, and shorter climbers may find it harder.
overview: A model route that favors taller climbers. Climb the face, then cut hard to the left up onto the arete and clip upward to the chains.

name: No Place Like Home
beta: Reach the alcove under the overhang by climbing the neighbouring route, then rock up onto the arete and fight your way along it, making awkward clips. Hanging the draws ahead of time helps.
overview: A classic arete, in plain sight from the road, with generous bolt spacing, technical moves and plenty of exposure.

current.area_walk_in: A short uphill walk of five to ten minutes on the trail leads to the base of the wall.

beta: A squat, blocky roof begins the route; above it a pocketed face leads to the chains over a shallow trough.
overview: Climbs over a low roof of blocky rock, then follows a pocketed face to anchors set over a shallow trough.

name: One Side Makes You Taller
beta: Climb the short flake, then step onto big plates and knobs, drifting leftward until you find a good rest. From there the edges shrink, so crimp harder all the way to the chains.
overview: A three-star sport line that starts up a little flake, then exits onto big plates and knobs and finishes on thinner edges.

name: Overlord
beta: Technical face climbing on solid crimps leads straight up to the anchors; stay on the bolted face and avoid the dirty crack beside it.
overview: Technical face climbing on dependable crimps all the way to the anchors; a fun, well-travelled sport line.

beta: Work leftward to get over the roof, protecting it with a sling around a block and horizontal placements. Continue up the wide crack, then step left to finish at the neighbouring route's anchors.
overview: A short crack route that is the first one you meet when walking along the wall, passing a roof and then a wide crack.

name: Physical Attraction
beta: The lower part is a grubby, moderate crack from offwidth to fist size that runs up to a shelf just short of the top. Above, an overhanging fist crack takes the final twenty feet, and a short chimney completes the route. Large gear is useful.
overview: A crack that varies in width: dirty and moderate in the lower portion, then an overhanging fist crack and a short chimney to finish.

beta: Start on a ledge with a difficult, sharp opening, then ascend a vertical face on gleaming hangers, crossing a brief pocketed stretch on the way to the chains.
overview: A tough, sharp opening off a ledge gives way to a vertical face with shiny bolt hangers, a short pocketed stretch, and then the chains.

overview: A broken finger crack that flares higher up and then gives way to an easy slab where protection is sparse.

name: The Proverbial Donkey
beta: Angle upward over the face into a fist-size crack splitting a roof, then follow the crack system across several ledges to a comfortable belay ledge below a large roof. Move out the roof with shaky jams and poor footholds, reaching chain anchors past the lip.
overview: A fist-width fissure in a ceiling is gained from the alcove by climbing the face, and a fall near the bottom could strike the boulder. A crack system then leads over ledges to a belay under a 15 ft roof; skip the roof for an easier 5.10b R finish, or jam out it on poor feet to the chains.

name: The Seventh Circle of Dante
beta: Begin from an enormous hueco and ascend the face, aiming for a wide crack. Follow the crack as it flares and then peters out, place gear in a pocket, and carry on across the slab to a rappel tree.
overview: From a large hueco the face leads into a broad crack that flares and then pinches out. Gear is placed from a pocket, and the slab above ends at a tree used for the abseil.
